newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Feb 17.

text.p: Teenagers in the northern Wellington suburbs of Whitby and Paremata were reeling on Sunday after a tragic weekend. They were struggling to come to terms with a friend's murder, a fatal car crash, a suicide and a drowning. Page One.

Morehu McDonald, the Aotearoa Television Network founding director who shared Tukoroirangi Morgan's liking for company-provided expensive clothes, was sacked by Television New Zealand in 1993 for dishonesty. According to further evidence put before the Employment Court that year by TVNZ, McDonald
admitted the seriousness of his behaviour and conceded it was sufficient to warrant dismissal. Page 1.

Costs in public hospitals have increased faster since they have become crown health enterprises than during their time under area health board rules, according to a consultant's report commissioned by the government. The report, Trends in Area Health Board/CHE Performance, also says real funding of boards or CHEs fell by 7.8 percent between 1989-90 and 1992-93, while real expenditure increased by two percent. Page 2.

Labour's women's affairs spokeswoman, Dianne Yates, intends to introduce a private members bill to enable parents to take six weeks' paid leave. She said on Sunday that the bill, which she hoped to have ready by the end of the month, would bring New Zealand into line with other Western countries. The bill would introduce six weeks' paid leave at a flat rate, available to either spouse. Page 2.

Listed petroleum investor New Zealand Petroleum has reported a 43 percent rise in its interim tax-paid oss to $723,000 for the six months to November 30. The result contrasts with a $505,000 loss reported for the previous corresponding period. It arose from unrealised portfolio losses since May of $462,000 the company said. Expenses of $186,000 had been contained within the forecast amount. Page 16.

Programming was not part of discussions between Independent Newspapers and Television New Zealand in TVNZ's proposal to raise its stake in pay TV operator Sky Network Television, TVNZ said on Sunday. TVNZ chief executive Chris Anderson has been reported in Australian media saying the company may spend up to A$70 million (NZ$78.10 million) raising its 16.3 percent stake to 20 percent or 25 percent. Page 16.

The New Zealand Salmon Company's 50 percent-owned joint venture in Chile, Aquacultivos, was moving to diversify from its dependence on the Japanese market, shareholders were told in Christchurch on Friday. Peter Townsend, a director of the Christchurch-based company and a former chief executive, told the company's annual meeting the Japenese market was soft for salmon and the salmon trout grown by Aquacultivos. Page 16.

Freedom International's new chief, Wayne Dodge, says he does not like the expression "business as usual" -- so expect changes in Hamilton's trans-Tasman airline. Dodge, an American, visited Hamilton last week, nine days after taking over from Freedom's founding general manager, Ric Macgillicuddy. Dodge said any changes would reflect his business manatra -- to give safe, clean, high quality service as cheaply as possible. "If we're not going to change, we're probably not responding to the market." Page 17.

Auckland-based Alpine Electronics has quadrupled its ability to supply overseas markets, with the opening of a $6 million electronic components plant in Mt Wellington. The plant will supply car audio systems to the global company's subsidiaries in Latin America, Australia, Europe and South America. Page 17.

The National Bank of New Zealand has reported a sharp fall in pre-tax profit to $130 million for the year ending December 31, 1996, from $201 million in 1995. After-tax profit was also down, at $97 million, compared with $158 million a year earlier. Page 17.
